kicker: Household savings · domestic flows vs foreign selling, Oct 2026
title: Households kept buying as foreign investors sold
dek: SIPs brought in ₹32,160 cr in October (+8.9% YoY) from 10 crore accounts, and equity funds had their 68th straight month of inflows, while foreign investors sold a net ₹2.95 lakh cr of Indian equities in Jan–Oct 2026.

chart.title: Where domestic money stood, October 2026
chart.sub: AMFI, depository and exchange data · year-on-year change where available

read: Domestic savers absorbed the year's foreign selling; the test is whether SIP growth, already slowed to single digits, holds if prices stay weak.
sources: AMFI monthly data (October 2026); CDSL and NSDL account statistics; NSDL/CDSL FPI data; BSE/NSE provisional institutional flow data; Vantage analysis
notes: Mutual fund figures are AMFI's for October 2026: SIP contributions ₹32,160 cr (₹32,490 cr in September), contributing SIP accounts 10.00 crore, SIP AUM ₹17.68 lakh cr, equity-scheme net inflows ₹32,994 cr, total AUM ₹83.39 lakh cr against ₹79.88 lakh cr a year earlier, and 28.78 crore folios. Demat accounts add CDSL's 19.63 crore and NSDL's 4.77 crore at end-October 2026; a person can hold several accounts, so this overstates unique investors. Foreign flows are net equity flows from depository data for January–October 2026; domestic institutional buying is the exchanges' provisional cash-market tally to 13 October (the latest full-period figure we could confirm) and covers mutual funds, insurers, banks and pension funds, not households alone. Equity fund assets rose only 5.6% in a year because prices fell while money kept coming in.
